mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) over the prior two months indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand that reduces corporate revenue expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline over the prior two months, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% year-over-year), a rise in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.1 percentage points over the prior month signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp in 1 month, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 persons signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5 percentage points from the prior month signals a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO falls > 0.5pp in 1 month, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month indicates a monetary policy response to inflation that increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS rise over the prior month, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of weak economic growth (GDPC1 annualized growth rate < 2.0%), a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) over the prior two months signals a contraction in consumer demand that reduces corporate revenue expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 annualized growth < 2.0% and RSAFS declines over the prior two months, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window remains below 0.03.
